passage:
The hostel computer lab was empty at 1 a.m. except for Yamini and the glow of a profile that wasn't hers.
"Anika, 21, loves sunsets and poetry" had a smile Yamini had copied from a stranger's travel photos. Anika had four hundred followers. Yamini, in real life, ate dinner alone most nights.
Lokesh, from the city college, messaged Anika every evening now. Tonight he wrote: "You're the only person I can be real with."
Yamini read it three times. It felt wonderful. It also felt like theft. He was being real with someone who didn't exist, and the girl who did exist was using his trust to feel admired.
He had asked twice for a video call. She had made excuses both times.
She opened a new message and typed, slowly: "There's something true I need to tell you about who I am." Her finger hovered over send.

qa.q: What did Lokesh write tonight?
qa.a: He wrote, "You're the only person I can be real with."

qa.q: Why did the message feel both wonderful and like theft to Yamini?
qa.a: It gave her the admiration she craved, but she knew Lokesh was trusting someone who didn't exist.

qa.q: What should Yamini do while her finger hovers over send?
qa.a: She should send it, tell Lokesh the truth plainly and apologise, and stop using the fake profile, even though it will hurt.

qa.q: How might Lokesh feel when he learns the truth?
qa.a: He may feel shocked, hurt and foolish for sharing so much, even though being deceived is not his fault.

grounding: A lonely student runs a false profile to feel admired, and sees she is using Lokesh's trust whatever her motive.

passage:
Dear Shalini,
For eight months you've known me as Nysa, the singer from Mumbai with the rooftop studio. There is no Nysa. There is no rooftop. I'm Bhavna, nineteen, I live with my parents in Bhopal, and I have never sung in front of anyone.
I made Nysa after a bad year when I felt invisible. The photos were a stranger's. The stories were things I wished were mine. When you started telling me about your exams and your father's illness, I should have stopped. Instead I kept going, because you admired her, and that felt like being admired myself.
Some people make profiles like this to take money, or worse. I didn't, but I still used your trust, and that is wrong whatever my reason.
I'm sorry. I've deleted the account. If you ever want to talk to the real me, I'm here.
Bhavna

qa.q: What persona did Bhavna invent?
qa.a: Bhavna invented Nysa, a singer from Mumbai with a rooftop studio.

qa.q: What did Bhavna feel when Shalini admired Nysa?
qa.a: It felt like being admired personally, which soothed the invisibility Bhavna had felt after a bad year.

qa.q: When should Bhavna have stopped, and what does the letter get right?
qa.a: Bhavna should have stopped when Shalini began sharing real worries; the letter tells the whole truth, deletes the account and admits the trust was used whatever the reason.

qa.q: What might Shalini feel reading this email?
qa.a: Shalini may feel shocked, embarrassed and betrayed after sharing personal things, and may need time before deciding whether to talk.

grounding: Bhavna confesses to inventing a glamorous online persona out of insecurity and admits that Shalini's trust was used regardless of the motive.

passage:
"Jomon, I need to tell you something and you're going to hate me."
"Try me."
"The profile Riddhi's been talking to for four months, 'Arjun from Bangalore'? That's me."
Jomon stared. "What?"
"I used a model's photos. I made up a job. I just… I was lonely after the move. And nobody talks to me here. But as 'Arjun,' she laughs at everything I say."
"Wasim. She told me yesterday she thinks she's in love with Arjun."
"I know." Wasim put his face in his hands. "I never wanted money or anything. I just wanted someone to like me."
"But she's trusting someone who doesn't exist. That's her trust you're using, whatever the reason."
"What do I do?"
"You tell her. The truth. Soon. And you shut the fake profile."
Wasim was quiet a long time. "Will you sit with me while I write it?"
"Yes."

qa.q: How long had Riddhi been talking to the profile?
qa.a: For four months.

qa.q: Why did Wasim make the fake profile?
qa.a: Wasim felt lonely and invisible after the move, and as "Arjun" he felt liked and admired.

qa.q: What did Jomon advise Wasim to do?
qa.a: Tell Riddhi the truth soon and shut the fake profile, and Jomon agreed to sit with him while he wrote it.

qa.q: How might Riddhi feel when she learns the truth?
qa.a: Riddhi would likely feel hurt, foolish and betrayed, since she believes she's in love with someone who doesn't exist.

grounding: It shows a young adult who invented a false online identity out of loneliness, and a friend naming that the other person's trust is being used regardless of motive.

passage:
I'm Tarun, and for most of my first year in college, I was someone else online.
I made a profile with a better face and a better life. I said I played guitar and had lived in London. I was lonely and felt ugly and boring, and this version of me got messages. One of them was from Gurleen, from another college. We talked every night for five months.
She told me real things. Her father's illness. Her fear of failing her exams. And I answered as someone who didn't exist.
Every time she asked for a video call, I made an excuse. I told myself I wasn't hurting anyone. I wasn't asking for money.
Then one night she wrote, "You're the only person I trust completely." I sat on the hostel floor feeling sick. Whatever my reasons, I was using that trust.
I told her the truth the next day. She blocked me. She had every right to.

qa.q: For how many months did Tarun and Gurleen talk every night?
qa.a: For five months.

qa.q: How did Tarun feel when Gurleen said he was the only person she trusted completely?
qa.a: Tarun felt sick and ashamed, realising that whatever the reasons, Gurleen's real trust was being used.

qa.q: What did Tarun do that was right, even though it cost him?
qa.a: Tarun told Gurleen the truth the next day and accepted that she blocked him.

qa.q: How might Gurleen feel after learning the truth?
qa.a: Gurleen would likely feel betrayed and foolish, having shared real fears about her father and exams with someone who didn't exist.

grounding: A young adult recalls hiding behind a false profile out of loneliness and insecurity, and realising the other person's trust was being used.

passage:
College counsellor's note, Friday.
Pallavi, second year, came in today, shaking. For three months she has been running a fake profile, a confident young man with a gym photo and a startup, and chatting with Madhuri, a classmate she barely speaks to in real life.
She said she started it as a joke, then kept going because Madhuri was so warm, and because she herself felt invisible in class. "She tells him things she'd never tell me."
Now Madhuri wants to meet "him" and has told other friends she's in a relationship. Pallavi said, "I didn't take money. I didn't mean harm." I told her that the motive matters, but Madhuri's trust has been used either way, and the kindest thing now is honesty.
We planned what she will say and agreed she will close the profile today. I've offered to support both students after Pallavi tells Madhuri on Monday.

qa.q: What photo did the fake profile use?
qa.a: A gym photo.

qa.q: What was Pallavi feeling that kept the fake profile going?
qa.a: Pallavi felt invisible in class, and Madhuri's warmth toward the fake man made her feel admired.

qa.q: What steps did the counsellor and Pallavi agree on?
qa.a: Pallavi will close the profile today and tell Madhuri the truth on Monday, and the counsellor will support both students.

qa.q: How might Madhuri feel when she learns the truth?
qa.a: Madhuri would likely feel hurt, embarrassed and betrayed, especially having told friends she was in a relationship.

grounding: A counsellor notes a young adult who created a false profile out of insecurity and used a classmate's trust, now preparing to tell the truth.

passage:
Thursday, late
Sumit sent a voice note tonight saying Naina is the only person who really gets him. Naina doesn't exist. I made her up three months ago, on a lonely night in this new city, with a borrowed photo and a life that sounded brighter than mine. I just wanted someone to reply to me with that kind of excitement.
And he did. He tells her about his exams, his dad's surgery, things his own friends don't know. With every message I feel warm for a minute and then sick. He's trusting a face that isn't mine.
I keep telling myself I'm not like the people who do this for money. But he's still being fooled, whatever my reasons are.
Tomorrow I'll write to him as me, Rekha, and tell him the truth before he shares one more thing. I'm terrified he'll hate me. He has every right to.
And I'm deleting the photo. It was never mine to use.

qa.q: How long ago did Rekha make up Naina?
qa.a: Three months ago.

qa.q: How does Rekha feel reading Sumit's messages?
qa.a: Rekha feels warm for a minute and then sick and guilty, knowing Sumit is trusting a face that isn't Rekha's.

qa.q: What is Rekha planning, and why is it right?
qa.a: Rekha plans to write as Rekha, tell Sumit the truth and delete the borrowed photo, stopping the deception before he shares more.

qa.q: What might Sumit feel when he learns the truth?
qa.a: Sumit may feel hurt, foolish and betrayed, since he shared his exams and his dad's surgery with someone he thought was Naina.

grounding: Shows a lonely young adult who invented an online identity to feel admired, and sees that the other person's trust is being used whatever the motive.
